proof:
Source: the first half of step 7 of the parent-supplied proof, in general form. This proof was kernel-checked during the decomposition review. Write O := (a, b) × (c, d), a measurable set.
1. Let p ∉ O. Either p.1 ∉ (a, b), so f(p.1) = 0, or p.2 ∉ (c, d), so ψ₀(p.2) = 0. Hence f(p.1)ψ₀(p.2)H(p) = 0 off O, and ∫_{ℝ²} f(p.1)ψ₀(p.2)H(p) dp = ∫_O f(p.1)ψ₀(p.2)H(p) dp (setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero).
2. By hypothesis, f(p.1)ψ₀(p.2)H(p) = (f(p.1)·h(p.1))·ψ₀(p.2) for a.e. p ∈ O. So the two set integrals over O agree (setIntegral_congr_ae, O measurable).
3. Lebesgue measure on ℝ² is volume.prod volume (Measure.volume_eq_prod). Apply setIntegral_prod_mul to the functions t ↦ f(t)h(t) and ψ₀; this identity holds without any integrability assumption. It gives ∫_O (f h)(p.1)·ψ₀(p.2) dp = (∫_{(a,b)} f(t)h(t) dt)·(∫_{(c,d)} ψ₀(α) dα).
4. ψ₀ = 0 off (c, d), so ∫_{(c,d)} ψ₀ = ∫_ℝ ψ₀ = 1. Likewise f·h = 0 off (a, b), so ∫_{(a,b)} f h = ∫_ℝ f h (setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero). Combining steps 1–4 gives ∫_{ℝ²} f(p.1)ψ₀(p.2)H(p) dp = ∫_ℝ f(t)h(t) dt. ∎
key_steps: The integrand vanishes off (a,b)×(c,d), so the integral equals the set integral over the box.
On the box, replace H(p) by h(p.1) a.e. (setIntegral_congr_ae).
setIntegral_prod_mul factors the box integral as (∫_{(a,b)} f h)·(∫_{(c,d)} ψ₀), with no integrability needed.
Both factors are whole-line integrals because f·h and ψ₀ vanish off the intervals; ∫ψ₀ = 1.
